records.title: What counts as big game
records.note: Wild pig is not on this list — § 375 makes it an exotic game mammal and § 377 gives it its own methods section.
records.verbatim: “Big game” means the following: deer (genus Odocoileus), elk (genus Cervus), pronghorn antelope (genus Antilocarpa), black bear (genus Ursus) and Nelson bighorn sheep (subspecies Ovis canadensis nelsoni) in the areas described in subsection 4902(b) of the Fish and Game Code.

records.title: Taking big game outside this section, and the nonlead requirement
records.note: Every method below is read together with the nonlead requirement in § 250.1.
records.verbatim: It shall be unlawful to take or attempt to take big game in violation of this section or Section 250.1. The take or attempted take of any big game (as defined by Section 350 of these regulations) with a firearm shall be in accordance with the use of nonlead projectiles and ammunition pursuant to Section 250.1 of these regulations.

records.title: What a projectile is, and what softnose or expanding means
records.note: A frangible bullet is excluded by name, so a cartridge that is on the list can still be loaded with a projectile that is not.
records.verbatim: Definition. For purposes of this section, a projectile is any bullet, ball, sabot, slug, buckshot or other device which is expelled from a firearm through a barrel by force. The following definitions shall apply: (1) A softnose or expanding projectile is a bullet designed to increase from its original diameter, commonly referred to as “mushrooming”, and retain a significant part of its original weight upon impact with, or when passing through the tissues of an animal. (2) Projectiles commonly referred to as “frangible” bullets, designed to disintegrate upon impact with, or when passing through the tissues of an animal are not softnose or expanding projectiles.

records.title: What may be used on big game

Anything this sentence does not name is not authorized for these animals, and the section states no minimum caliber for a centerfire rifle.
records.verbatim: Except for the provisions of the following subsections (d) through (j), big game may only be taken by rifles using centerfire cartridges with softnose or expanding projectiles; bow and arrow (see Section 354 of these regulations for archery equipment regulations); or wheellock, matchlock, flintlock or percussion type, including “in-line” muzzleloading rifles using black powder or equivalent black powder substitute, including pellets, with a single projectile loaded from the muzzle and at least .40 caliber in designation.

records.title: Lights, night vision and optics
records.note: Laser rangefinders, red-dot scopes and fiberoptic sights are named as permitted; night vision and sniperscopes are named as prohibited and may not even be possessed.
records.verbatim: Except as otherwise provided, while taking or attempting to take big game under the provisions of this section or Section 354 of these regulations it is unlawful to use any device or devices which: 1) throw, cast or project an artificial light or electronically alter or intensify a light source for the purpose of visibly enhancing an animal; or 2) throw, cast or project an artificial light or electronically alter or intensify a light source for the purpose of providing a visible point of aim directly on an animal. Devices commonly referred to as “sniperscopes”, night vision scopes or binoculars, or those utilizing infra-red, heat sensing or other non-visible spectrum light technology used for the purpose of visibly enhancing an animal or providing a visible point of aim directly on an animal are prohibited and may not be possessed while taking or attempting to take big game. Devices commonly referred to as laser rangefinders, “red-dot” scopes with self-illuminating reticles, and fiberoptic sights with self-illuminating sight or pins which do not throw, cast or project a visible light onto an animal are permitted.

records.title: A loaded muzzleloader in a vehicle
records.note: The section defines when a muzzleloading firearm counts as loaded, and the definition is broader than most people expect.
records.verbatim: Unless provided in these regulations or any other law, it is unlawful to possess a loaded muzzleloading firearm in any vehicle or conveyance or its attachments which is standing on or along or is being driven on or along any public road or highway or other way open to the public. For the purposes of this section, a muzzleloading firearm shall be deemed to be loaded when it is capped or primed or has an electronic or other ignition device attached and has a powder charge and projectile or shot in the barrel or cylinder.

records.title: What nonlead means, and the one percent figure

records.verbatim: Definitions (1) A projectile is any bullet, ball, sabot, slug, buckshot, shot, pellet or other device that is expelled from a firearm through a barrel by force. (2) Nonlead ammunition is any centerfire, shotgun, muzzleloading, or rimfire ammunition containing projectiles certified pursuant to subsection (b)(3) or subsection (f). (3) Shotgun ammunition containing pellets composed of materials approved as nontoxic by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, as identified in Section 507.1 of these regulations, is considered certified. (4) A nonlead projectile shall contain no more than one percent lead by weight, as certified pursuant to subsection (b)(3) or subsection (f).

(3) Nothing in this section is intended to prohibit the possession of concealable firearms containing lead ammunition, provided that the firearm is possessed for personal protection and is not used to take or assist in the take of wildlife.

in_season_notice.headline: The underlying statute was amended and this regulation has not been updated
in_season_notice.body: AB 1912 (Hadwick) was signed on 27 August 2026 and amends Fish and Game Code § 4370, the statute the Fish and Game Commission gave as its reason for limiting the § 354(h)(1) concealed-firearm exception to big game other than deer. 14 CCR § 354(h) has not been amended and still reads as quoted above. The operative date of the statute could not be verified from an official source, so this app states none. Verify with CDFW before you carry a firearm during an archery deer season.

conditions.headline: We cannot tell you whether this is legal where you are
conditions.body: § 353(d) allows size 0 or 00 buckshot for deer only in areas where a county ordinance prohibits the discharge of rifles or shotguns with slugs. This app does not carry county ordinances. Read § 353(d) and check with the county.

conditions.headline: We cannot tell you whether this is legal where you are
conditions.body: § 377(d) allows size 0 or 00 buckshot only in areas where a county ordinance prohibits the discharge of rifles or shotguns with slugs. This app does not carry county ordinances. Read § 377(d) and check with the county.

conditions.headline: Sooty and ruffed grouse only, and only in named counties
conditions.body: § 311(m) is the only sentence in § 311 that adds a pistol or revolver for a bird, and it names sooty and ruffed grouse. For quail, chukar and other partridges, pheasant, ptarmigan, sage grouse and wild turkey, no subsection of § 311 authorizes a pistol or revolver at all. Where it does apply, § 311(m) names the counties and the season by pointing at § 300(a)(1)(E), which is published as a map image rather than as text this app can read. Read § 311(m) and § 300(a)(1)(E).

conditions.headline: We cannot tell you whether this is legal where you are
conditions.body: § 377(f) is the only crossbow sentence in § 377, and it is written as a restriction: a crossbow may not be used to take exotic game mammals in an area where an archery season is open for deer, elk or pronghorn antelope. Whether that describes where and when you are hunting depends on the area and the date, and this app does not resolve it. Read § 377(f) and the seasons for that area.

conditions.headline: Not in Los Angeles County
conditions.body: § 311(g) authorizes rifles and pistols for rabbits and squirrels statewide except in Los Angeles County, where it says rifles and pistols may not be used. Read § 311(g).

conditions.headline: Nothing larger than 12 gauge at Morro Bay
conditions.body: § 507(a)(4) allows 10 gauge or smaller statewide, except in areas open to hunting on, over or adjacent to the waters of Morro Bay, San Luis Obispo County, where it says no shotgun larger than 12 gauge shall be used. Read § 507(a)(4).

conditions.headline: At least .40 caliber in designation
conditions.body: § 353(c) names a single projectile loaded from the muzzle and at least .40 caliber in designation. A muzzleloader below that is measured against the sentence itself.

conditions.headline: At least .40 caliber in designation
conditions.body: § 377(c) names a single projectile loaded from the muzzle and at least .40 caliber in designation. A muzzleloader below that is measured against the sentence itself.

conditions.headline: Three shells is the ceiling
conditions.body: § 353(d) authorizes shotguns capable of holding not more than three shells. This app does not carry magazine capacities and cannot check yours — the sentence that states the limit is quoted below.

conditions.headline: Three shells is the ceiling
conditions.body: § 377(d) authorizes shotguns capable of holding not more than three shells. This app does not carry magazine capacities and cannot check yours — the sentence that states the limit is quoted below.

conditions.headline: At least a 4-inch barrel
conditions.body: § 353(f) authorizes pistols and revolvers with minimum barrel lengths of 4 inches, using centerfire cartridges with softnose or expanding projectiles. This app does not carry barrel lengths and cannot measure yours; § 353(f) requires 4 inches and is quoted below. § 353(e), for deer and bear, names no barrel length at all.

conditions.headline: Softnose or expanding projectiles
conditions.body: § 353(c) and § 353(e) authorize centerfire cartridges with softnose or expanding projectiles. § 353(b) defines those as bullets designed to increase from their original diameter and retain a significant part of their original weight, and says projectiles commonly referred to as frangible are not among them. This app does not know what is in your ammunition.

conditions.headline: Softnose or expanding projectiles
conditions.body: § 377(c) and § 377(e) authorize centerfire cartridges with softnose or expanding projectiles. § 377(b) defines those as bullets designed to increase from their original diameter and retain a significant part of their original weight, and says projectiles commonly referred to as frangible are not among them. This app does not know what is in your ammunition.

conditions.headline: No shot larger than No. BB — and No. 2 for wild turkey
conditions.body: § 311(b) forbids using or possessing a shell containing shot larger than No. BB, except that shot larger than No. 2 may not be used or possessed when taking wild turkey. All shot must be loose in the shell. This app does not know which shell is in your gun.

conditions.headline: At least a 0.177 caliber pellet for wild turkey
conditions.body: § 311(f) authorizes an air rifle used with any caliber of pellet, except that wild turkey may only be taken with a pellet that is at least 0.177 caliber.

conditions.headline: Flu-flu fletching
conditions.body: § 507(a)(2) allows only arrows and crossbow bolts with flu-flu fletching, except that conventionally fletched arrows may be used to take waterfowl sitting on the water from scull boats or similar watercraft.
